markdown_content: ## Overview of Trim Improvements in CLO 2025.0 This section covers the new and improved methods for adding and manipulating trims in CLO 2025.0, including the use of the glue bottle, looping trims through fabric, CPU vs GPU simulation limitations, and the introduction of the tack tool to attach multiple points on trims for better control and realism. --- ## Methods for Adding and Simulating Trims Trims in CLO can be added and manipulated in several ways: - **Using the Glue Bottle Tool**: Select a trim and use the glue bottle tool to attach it to a garment piece, then run simulation to see it behave naturally. - **Looping Trims Through Fabric**: A new feature allows trims to be pulled through sections of fabric. This involves selecting the trim, right-clicking to activate the option, and simulating to see it fall and loop through the fabric realistically. ### CPU vs GPU Simulation for Trims - The looping trims feature **only works on CPU simulation**. If you switch to GPU simulation, the trim looping will deactivate and fail to simulate properly. - When on GPU, the option to activate looping is greyed out. - For best results when using looping or tack tools, keep simulation mode set to CPU. --- ## Using the Tack Tool to Attach Multiple Points on Trims The **tack tool** is a significant improvement for controlling trims by allowing users to attach multiple points for a more precise fit. ### How to Use the Tack Tool 1. Select the trim. 2. Activate the tack tool or edit tack tool. 3. Click on desired points on the trim to create tacks. When placed correctly, tacks turn red (default color is purple). 4. You can add as many tacks as needed to secure the trim to the garment. ### Adjusting Tack Points - If tacks are misplaced, use the edit tack tool to move them. - Adjusting your camera perspective helps align tacks accurately, especially by viewing from underneath or other angles to line points perfectly. - This improves trim fitting and reduces simulation issues. --- ## Practical Tips for Tack Tool Usage and Trim Adjustment - If selecting or aligning trims is difficult, move the trim out, adjust the tack points, then reposition the trim using the gizmo tool. - Always simulate after setting or adjusting tacks to see the real-time effect. - You can freeze trims to lock their position temporarily and fine-tune the fit. - Use right-click to activate, deactivate, or strengthen trims to manage their simulation state and resolve conflicts. - Deactivating problematic tacks or trims and simulating again can help fix simulation conflicts caused by sewing, collision, or overlapping meshes. --- ## Troubleshooting Trim Simulation Issues - Complex trims with multiple tacks or tight fitting may cause simulation errors or conflicts. - If trims behave erratically, try deactivating them, simulating, and then reactivating once the garment settles. - Use the freeze and unfreeze options strategically to isolate and adjust problematic areas. - Patience and iterative adjustments often lead to a successful simulation setup. --- ## Advanced Trim Closure Control Using Tack String Length CLO allows users to fine-tune the closure tightness of trims through the **tack string length** parameter: - Access this by selecting the tack and choosing "Edit Tack." - Adjust the **tack string length** value from 1 to 10. - Lower values provide a looser closure. - Higher values (up to 10) pull the trim tighter for a more secure fit. - Simulate after adjusting to observe how the trim tightens or loosens. This feature enables realistic fake closures and enhanced trim fitting. --- ## Summary CLO 2025.0 introduces enhanced trim features, including: - Multiple ways to add trims (glue bottle, looping through fabric). - A critical distinction that looping trims only simulate on CPU, not GPU. - The powerful tack tool for attaching multiple points, improving fit and realism. - Adjustable tack string length for fine-tuning closure tightness. - Best practices for simulation include toggling activation states, freezing/unfreezing trims, and adjusting tacks iteratively to resolve conflicts. These improvements provide users with more control and flexibility when working with trims, leading to better garment realism and easier troubleshooting during design.
